To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose two novel consensus filters for distributed tracking in camera networks, and show by simulations that the proposed consensus filters outperform existing consensus filters in terms of estimation accuracy, convergence speed and computational complexity.

the EICF and EIWCF are two distributed consensus-based non-linear algorithms to track highly maneuvering targets in wireless camera networks that outperform the related work by achieving higher accuracy with faster convergence.
we proposed two consensus-based distributed non-linear algorithms, EICF and EIWCF, for tracking in wireless camera sensor networks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
distributed non-linear estimation and consensus-based target tracking in wireless camera sensor networks.
the design and analysis of consensus protocols for distributed target tracking in wireless camera sensor networks.
developing distributed consensus-based algorithms for target tracking in wireless camera network that can overcome the problems of non-linearity, naivety, and redundancy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithms outperform all the existing distributed non-linear consensus algorithms in terms of both accuracy and speed of convergence.
EICF is a better solution when the target is not maneuvering and EIWCF is a better solution in general.
EIWCF outperforms the EICF and the related state of art in the sense that it provides the most accurate estimates in the fastest time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed algorithms are able to track highly maneuvering targets in a wireless camera network in the presence of naivety, redundancy, non-linearity and measurement loss.
the EICF and the EIWCF can handle the naivety problem and the non-linearity problem respectively.
the EICF algorithm is more suitable for large camera networks (Nc is not available) and the EIWCF algorithm is more suitable in small networks (Nc available).
The main takeaway from our work is that
consensus protocols can be used to handle the non-linearities in the measurement model and the effect of naivity and redundancy in distributed tracking in camera networks.
the proposed consensus-based algorithms can be used in a distributed setting to achieve the same accuracy as the centralised approach.
the proposed consensus filters can handle the non-linearities in the camera measurement models and can be used for tracking highly maneuvering targets in a wireless camera network.
